etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: Perhaps from Middle English cotsete, from Old English cotsǣta (“cottager”), from cot (“cottage”) (Modern English cot (“cottage”) (archaic)) + -sǣta (“-sitter”); compare coscet. Compare German Hauslamm (literally “house lamb”), Italian casiccio.
senses: (transitive) To treat like a pet; to overly indulge. [from 1650s]
(transitive) To fondle; to touch or stroke lovingly.
A pet, usually a pet lamb. [from 1570s]

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: Alternative form of cossid (“courier or messenger”).
